title: The Breathing Cure
author: Patrick McKeown
blurb: This is a massive tome on all things breathing. You can read it start-to-finish, or use it as a reference whenever you’re interested in a specific topic. There’s even a section on diabetes featuring yours truly 😊

title: The Science of Enlightenment
author: Shinzen Young
blurb: The title made me hesitant for a long time, but it surprised me how good this book was. It’s one I suspect I’ll revisit every few years to understand it even more deeply.

title: Stolen Focus
author: Johann Hari
blurb: An awesome look at why we can’t concentrate. Hari combines research, interviews, and a 3-month phone-free experiment to show how we can begin to reclaim our focus.

title: Relaxation Revolution
author: Herbert Benson, MD
blurb: A foundational book in the mind–body world, providing the science and stories on how the relaxation response heals.

title: The Things You Can See Only When You Slow Down
author: Haemin Sunim
blurb: This is an easy-reading, poetic, and practical book on mindful living. If you’re drawn to contemplative practices, you’ll certainly be happy you added this one to your library.

title: Biofeedback and Mindfulness in Everyday Life
author: Inna Khazan, Ph.D
blurb: Although I’m not a huge fan of biofeedback personally, this is an excellent book on breathing, mindfulness, and their application in everyday life. It also has a great basic physiology section, written in an accessible way. Definitely worth the read if you want to nerd out a little.

title: How To Be Better At (Almost) Everything
author: Pat Flynn
blurb: Does this have a cheesy title? Yes. But is it still one of my favorites of all time? Definitely. I read it about 6 years ago, and it had a huge impact on my life. If you love learning, make sure you check this one out 👏

title: The Tibetan Yoga of Breath
author: Anyen Rinpoche & Allison Choying Zangmo
blurb: An excellent book on the healing power of breathing (or as they call it, “wind energy training”). It blends wisdom with practical exercises you can start using right away. I definitely recommend it.

title: The Oxygen Advantage
author: Patrick McKeown
blurb: This one doesn’t need much explanation. If you’ve had it on your reading (or re-reading) list, here’s a nudge to pick it up.

title: The No-Nonsense Meditation Book
author: Steven Laureys, MD
blurb: This is a great book on the science of meditation (along with many fun anecdotes and practical suggestions). There’s even a whole chapter on breathing 😊

title: The Healing Power of Mindfulness
author: Jon Kabat-Zinn, Ph.D
blurb: This is another excellent mindfulness book from Kabat-Zinn. I’d still recommend Full Catastrophe Living first, but this is a great follow-up, grounded in both science and practicality.

title: Blue Mind
author: Wallace J Nichols
blurb: While this one isn’t about breathing or meditation per se , it’s an excellent book on the power of water (and nature more broadly) to help us naturally cultivate mindfulness. As a surfer and someone who loves the ocean, it’s one of my all-time favorites.

title: Three Steps to Awakening
author: Larry Rosenberg
blurb: This is a great book on breath and meditation. The first two steps (Breath Awareness and Breath as an Anchor) are full of wisdom on the power of breathing, both literally and metaphorically. Definitely worth reading.

title: The Healing Power of Meditation
author: Andy Fraser (ed.)
blurb: This excellent book explores the scientific and practical benefits of meditation. Each chapter is written by a different expert, making it fun to read. Topics include telomerase, gray matter, adaptive functioning, and emotional health. An interesting and highly recommended read.

title: Full Catastrophe Living
author: Jon Kabat-Zinn, Ph.D
blurb: This is the classic text on Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR). It’s full of wisdom on breathing, mindfulness, and healing. A must-read for anyone interested in the contemplative sciences.

title: Altered Traits
author: Daniel Goleman, Ph.D. & Richard Davidson, Ph.D
blurb: I loved this one. It’s a clear, balanced look at what science actually says about meditation. If you enjoy nerding out on contemplative practice, I highly recommend it.

title: Elegant Simplicity
author: Satish Kumar
blurb: Kumar once walked 8,000 miles with no money in his pocket for a cause he believed in…crazy. That ‘be the change’ pilgrimage spirit carries through to this book. He lays out how to simplify your life—not just materially, but also mentally and spiritually, too.

title: Mindfulness in Plain English
author: Bhante Gunaratana
blurb: This book is an excellent foundational resource on meditation and mindfulness. I had to read it three times to fully appreciate how good it is. I definitely recommend it.

title: Spinal Breathing Pranayama
author: Yogani
blurb: Even if you don’t practice “spinal breathing pranayama,” this is a great read. It offers many practical guidelines and lots of wisdom on the breath. Definitely worth checking out if you enjoy slow breathing.

title: Peace is Every Breath
author: Thich Nhat Hanh
blurb: Every Thich Nhat Hanh book is worth reading, but I found this one especially powerful (and lyrical) in its exploration of the breath & mindfulness. Definitely worth checking out.

title: Breathwalk
author: Gurucharan Singh Khalsa, Ph.D., and Yogi Bhajan, Ph.D
blurb: Breathwalk is an all-in-one practice combining breathing, meditation, and physical movement. The book includes many specific routines you can try immediately, along with the philosophy and science behind why they work. Definitely worth the read.

title: Sovereign
author: Emma Seppälä, Ph.D
blurb: This is a great book filled with wisdom on taking control of and shaping our lives. It’s also got a ton of good information on the transformational power of breathing (and especially on the science of SKY breathing). Definitely a valuable read.

title: Heart Breath Mind
author: Leah Lagos, Psy.D
blurb: This is an excellent read on the power of slow breathing to train our hearts for better performance and less stress. If you’re into optimal performance—or just love applied breath science—definitely check it out.

title: 52 Ways to Walk
author: Annabel Streets
blurb: I loved this book. It’s a perfect blend of science and practical wisdom on all aspects of walking. Several chapters even discuss the benefits of controlled, nasal breathing while out on a stroll. It’s definitely an excellent read if you enjoy a good walk.

title: How God Changes Your Brain
author: Andrew Newberg, MD, and Mark Waldman
blurb: Don't let the title (or New Age-y cover) distract you. This book is actually more like “The Neuroscience of Meditation and Breathing.” A good portion of it focuses on contemplative practices and breathing exercises. It’s a fun and interesting read.

title: Falling Upward
author: Richard Rohr
blurb: This is one of my all-time favorites. It’s not about breathing or meditation per se, but full of wisdom for living a mindful and fulfilling life. Can’t recommend this one enough.

title: Natural Meditation
author: Dean Sluyter
blurb: I just finished this one and loved it. Simple, natural techniques alongside deep (yet super relatable) wisdom. It’s meditation for regular people.

title: The Stress Prescription
author: Elissa Epel, Ph.D
blurb: This is an excellent book if you’re dealing with stress and uncertainty—who isn’t? It’s filled with several great breathing gems and other simple practices for, as the subtitle says, “more joy and ease.”

title: Take Your Time
author: Eknath Easwaran
blurb: This is one of the first books I read by Easwaran, and the one that immediately made him my favorite teacher (I’ve now read 10 of his books!). It’s so good. If you’re like me and always rushing, always “ready for the next thing,” I highly recommend it.

title: Breathing: The Master Key to Self Healing
author: Andrew Weil, MD
blurb: This audiotape, released more than 20 years ago, is one of my top 5 recommendations for anyone beginning with breathing. It’s less than 2 hours and has almost everything we need to start a breath practice. Check it out if you haven’t already.

title: Dialed In
author: Dr. Dana Sinclair
blurb: My good friend and mentor Paul Hunt (whose MBSR course I occasionally share) recommended this one to me. It’s fantastic: Super practical and filled with many gems on the power of breathing.

title: The Coffee Bean
author: Jon Gordon and Damon West
blurb: I read this book this past Friday afternoon. It’s so good . Given that coffee is more important to me than oxygen 😂, I’m not sure how it took me this long to hear about it. It’s super short, so I won’t spoil it—just do yourself a favor and pick it up.

title: Tiny Habits
author: BJ Fogg, Ph.D
blurb: This is my favorite book on habits. It truly changed my life about 4 years ago. When it comes to breathing, meditation, or anything else that makes us better, the practices are usually straightforward. The hardest part is consistency. This book makes that part easy.

title: Still the Mind: An Introduction to Meditation
author: Alan Watts
blurb: This book offers a nice mix of philosophy and practical wisdom on meditation and breathing. I highly recommend the audio version, as it allows you to hear Watts speak, which brings life and humor to the words.

title: Don’t Believe Everything You Think
author: Joseph Nguyen
blurb: James Clear had this book on his list of three books he’d recommend to new graduates. And now I know why…it’s so good. It’s short, easy to read, and full of wisdom. It’s a perfect introduction to the world of contemplative practices.

title: Hidden Potential
author: Adam Grant
blurb: My good friend Mary Hunt recommended this one to me ( check out her coaching here ). I’ve taken a break from these types of books lately to mainly read about meditation and breathing, but this one was amazing. It’s a joy to read, full of studies, stories, and practical wisdom that you can immediately start applying.

title: Instructions for Spiritual Living
author: Paul Brunton
blurb: I was surprised how much I liked this book. Despite its rather terrible name, Brunton avoids cookie-cutter advice and instead offers genuine wisdom and practical advice on using contemplative practices to lead a better life.

title: How Bad Do You Want It?
author: Matt Fitzgerald
blurb: A detour from our usual breathing and meditation books, this was one of my all-time favorites on the mind, written through the lens of endurance sports. It’s filled with inspiring stories and fascinating science that’ll have you rethink what you’re capable of.

title: Breath Taking
author: Micheal J Stephen, MD
blurb: I loved this book because it’s not about “breathwork” but about “the breath.” I’ve joked that Dr. Stephen is the Feynman of the lungs, weaving poetic quotes into rigorous and fascinating scientific discussion. My favorite chapters were the Prologue, 1–4, and 12. It’s a great read for anyone interested in breathing.

title: The Healing Power of the Breath
author: Richard Brown, MD, and Patricia Gerbarg, MD
blurb: This is one of my all-time favorite books on breathing. It blends the essential science of breath with clear, practical instructions (and is just a joy to read). Brown and Gerbarg are truly a gift to the world of breathing and psychiatry.

title: The Mind Illuminated
author: John Yates, Ph.D., Matthew Immergut, Ph.D., and Jeremy Graves
blurb: This is an incredible book on the stages of meditation. I absolutely loved the first half or so…after that, a lot of it was beyond my understanding (simply because I haven’t progressed that far in my practice). However, I highly recommend it to anyone interested in the mind and its transformations through meditation.

title: The Heroic Heart
author: Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo
blurb: I got this book solely because it had the best title ever, lol, and I ended up absolutely loving it. This quote sums up its core message perfectly: “The important thing is not to worry about what is going to happen to us but to create inner strength to deal with whatever does happen.”

title: Do Walk
author: Libby DeLana
blurb: This one instantly became my favorite book on walking. It’s short, easy to read, and overflowing with wisdom on the power of walking. I can’t recommend it enough, and I hope it inspires you to walk more like it did me.

title: Awareness
author: Anthony de Mello
blurb: This is one of my favorites in the recent past. De Mello’s wisdom was genuinely life-changing for me. Also, I highly recommend the audiobook version— he’s hilarious , and reading the words doesn’t do it justice. (I often randomly put it on while walking because it’s so funny and full of wisdom that it never gets old.) I hope you’ll check it out!

title: The Well-Lived Life
author: Gladys McGarey, MD
blurb: I’ve been raving about this book for over a year now—it’s one of my all-time favorites. I’ve received more messages from readers that this book changed their life than any other I’ve shared. Dr. McGarey was 102 when she wrote it, and you can truly feel her wisdom in every sentence. (She has since passed away, back in September, at the age of 103.) I can’t recommend this one enough.

title: Move
author: Caroline Williams
blurb: Here’s another book I can’t recommend enough . If you’re curious about how movement affects your mind, it’s a must-read. Williams even has a whole chapter on breathing— the most fundamental movement —which is worth getting the book for by itself. Check it out if it sounds interesting!

title: Meditations for Mortals
author: Oliver Burkeman
blurb: I can’t recommend this one enough . Reading the introduction was my favorite part, as it felt like Burkeman was expressing thoughts I’ve had but never known how to articulate. I’ve never felt so much resonance with a book. Check it out if it sounds interesting to you!

title: Healing Through Breathing
author: Eddie Stern
blurb: This is a short, practical guide to the power of breathing for healing our bodies and minds. It blends science with ancient wisdom to offer plenty of simple yet powerful advice. It also includes guided breathing to get you started. Can’t recommend it enough. ( Note: It is only on Audible. )

title: Passage Meditation
author: Eknath Easwaran
blurb: If you’re tired of reading the same old things about meditation, here’s an approach I can almost promise you haven’t encountered. And even if you don’t adopt Easwaran’s 8-point program, his profound yet practical wisdom is sure to change how you think and live 🙏

title: Peak Mind
author: Amishi Jha, Ph.D
blurb: This is an incredible book on attention and mindfulness from one of the world’s leading researchers on the topics. If you want to learn how attention actually works—and how to train it—this is a must-read.

title: Breath by Breath
author: Larry Rosenberg
blurb: Even if you’re not into meditation, this book is worth the read for all the great quotes, stories, and analogies about the breath. It’s one of the first “non-breathwork” breathing books I read many years ago that opened my eyes to the power of the breath as an analogy for life.
